messages:
emma: opened a small docs PR to add compatibility notes and a short SDK example for the new celeste-9b model card. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/6012

emma: summary: celeste-9b-lite (q4_cpu) does not support 32k context KV cache; fallback to disk-cache increases tail latency. changes: (1) add a compatibility row to the model card, (2) paste a tiny p95 benchmark at 8k/32k contexts, (3) include short Python/JS snippets showing runtime.fallback detection and routing hint to prefer fp16-full for streaming.

josh: quick context from runtime: celeste-9b-lite uses host-mapped weights and we turn off on-GPU KV cache at >8k to avoid OOM. fallback path is expected. we should name the metric kernel.fallback_reason in the docs (that's what tracing emits).

rafael: bench I ran: ctx=8192 -> p95 tokens/sec: q4_cpu: 2.0 t/s, fp16-full: 6.8 t/s; ctx=32768 -> q4_cpu falls back and p95 latency rises ~4x. I'll paste a compact table in the PR.

emma: added short table and the compatibility row: "KV cache: not available on celeste-9b-lite variants at >8k; streaming may fallback to disk-cache worker (kernel.fallback_reason)." also added a one-line billing note: "Hosted customers: billing per-token unchanged; expect higher tail-latency and potential increased cost from longer worker time."

maya: small lint: the anchor you used "compatibility-notes" collides with several other cards. prefer model-scoped anchor like "celeste9b-compat".

lint-bot: ERROR docs/models/celeste-9b.md: anchor "compatibility-notes" already defined in docs/models/vega13b.md line 19.

emma: changed anchor to "celeste9b-compat" and pushed.

emma: Python snippet added to PR:```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient()
resp = c.generate(
    model="celeste-9b",
    input="<very long prefix>",
    routing={"prefer_variant": "fp16-full", "allow_fallback": True}
)
if resp.metadata.get("kernel.fallback_reason"):
    print("fallback used:", resp.metadata["kernel.fallback_reason"])```

emma: JS streaming example (tiny):```js
const client = new RedwoodClient();
const stream = await client.stream({ model: 'celeste-9b', routing: { prefer_variant: 'fp16-full' } });
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  if (chunk.meta && chunk.meta['kernel.fallback_reason']) {
    console.warn('fallback:', chunk.meta['kernel.fallback_reason'])
  }
  process.stdout.write(chunk.text)
}
```

rafael: runtime nit: recommend the docs say the specific variants: celeste-9b-q4_cpu, celeste-9b-q4_cpu-smallmap may exhibit fallback. also add a link to the catalog fallback table.

josh: added a one-sentence suggestion for the model card compatibility row: "Streaming: best-effort on lite variants; prefer non-lite for deterministic token boundaries and lower tail-latency."

emma: updated per comments, linked the kernel metric docs and catalog fallback table. pushed changes. docs-bot: please deploy preview.

lint-bot: re-run: no anchor duplicates found. small markdown warn: line-length in docs/models/celeste-9b.md line 72.

docs-bot: preview deployed for PR #6012 1 https://deploy-preview.docs/6012 1 view model card under "Compatibility".

maya: I'll smoke test the snippets in node/python and check wording. josh, can you confirm billing sentence is okay?

josh: billing phrasing fine.

maya: smoke: python snippet runs locally and metadata appears as kernel.fallback_reason. JS snippet works in modern node; left one small polyfill note for older node versions.

emma: thanks everyone 1 merging after maya's smoke. follow-ups: rafael to add bench to internal bench repo, josh to note billing in release notes.

emma: closing this thread after merge.
